samples.excerpt: ## What's new in 1.1.0 ### Sessions - **Model profiles**: a named token budget (Z-Image 400, Flux 512, Krea 2 512, Qwen-Image 1024, SDXL 75, or your own number). The linter and the engine's guard read the same string, so the warning and the trim always match. SDXL flips the prompt to comma tags on its own. - **Prompt template editor**: the sentence the engine fills, slot by slot ({style} {expression} {framing} {focus} {scene} {lighting} {person} {pose} {outfit} {placement} {quality}). A custom slot order for exotic encoders is one edit; the reset button restores the stock order; the linter flags unknown slots. LIVE TEXT now fills the template the way the engine does, instead of a rough draft. - **Keepers in the results dock**: star the good frames, press the re-shoot button, and everything you did not star gets a fresh take that lands back in its own slot. The wall survives re-shoots now. - **Pre-flight conflict warnings**: the swaps the engine would make silently, said out loud before the GPU pays for them. A face focus does not survive figure-tier crops, a back-to-camera pose reads the silhouette, a walked format feed drops the ratios the picked crops contradict. Each warning names the values and the swap. - **The inspiration roll**: one click re-rolls every creative section. The persona, the trigger, your own words, the negative and the session stay untouched, and the whole roll is one undo step. ### Character and sharing - **Character cards**: the whole persona plus the LoRA trigger under a name, saved in the ComfyUI user folder, one click to switch characters. - **Preset export and import**: presets download as .json files and load back, so setups move between installs. - **Ready-made looks**: eight curated full looks (clean girl, y2k crop, street layer, office sharp, cozy evening, night out, sporty set, goth edge), each styling hair, makeup and the first look's outfit in one click. ### Reading the session - **The arc's expression route**: with a dramaturgy arc

Basic Python functions for manipulating data that every programmer is used to, lightweight with no additional dependencies.

Supported data types:

samples.title: basic_data_handling
samples.excerpt: Backward compatible changes: - "save IMAGE to file" and "save IMAGE+MASK to file" can now be used like ComfyUI's built-in "Save Image" node: images written into the output (or temp) folder are reported back to the frontend, so the node shows a preview of what it saved and the images appear in ComfyUI's generated-images list. In addition both nodes got a second `images` output that passes the images through unchanged, like the built-in node does. - files written somewhere else (plain `path` mode) are still saved, they just cannot be previewed, as ComfyUI can only serve files from its own folders - Both save nodes now embed ComfyUI's workflow metadata (the API prompt and the full workflow) in addition to the existing prompt metadata. Dragging a saved file back onto the canvas therefore restores the workflow, while the explicitly given `prompt` / `negative_prompt` remain in the `parameters` text that image viewers display and that is easy to extract afterwards. This is what makes the two channels worth having when a whole batch is saved from a data list: the workflow then contains every prompt of the graph, whereas `parameters` always holds the prompt of the image that was actually written. - ComfyUI's `--disable-metadata` option suppresses both channels, exactly like it does for the built-in save node - No widget was added, removed or reordered, so existing workflows keep their saved widget values.
